That’s the trap: the smaller sentence opens a door you don’t feel ready to walk through. But you don’t have to choose between “nothing” and “the whole thing falling out” in that exact second.

You can answer his “what was it?” with a holding sentence, not the content: “I do want to tell you. I’m not dodging — I just want to say it when I’m not going to botch it. Give me until we’re in the car tonight.” That keeps the door open without dumping everything on the driveway.

And if the whole thing does fall out — messy, out of order — is that actually the disaster? Or is the scary part his reaction, or yours?

What’s the worst version of it falling out?
